biological.citation: Essential role for Bclaf1 in lung development and immune system function. (PMID: 19008920)
biological.summary: Bclaf1 knockout mice demonstrate that Bclaf1 is required for proper spatial and temporal organization of smooth muscle lineage during the saccular stage of lung development and is essential for peripheral T-cell homeostasis. Despite its postulated role as a proapoptotic protein, Bclaf1-deficient cells showed no defect in cell death linked to development or after exposure to apoptotic stimuli. These findings establish a critical role for Bclaf1 in developmental processes independent of apoptosis.

biological.citation: BCLAF1 restrains stress responses in hematopoietic stem cells to support expansion and repopulation. (PMID: 40435510)
biological.summary: Using hematopoietic-specific and inducible deletion of Bclaf1 in mice, BCLAF1 was found to promote fetal HSC development and is required for self-renewal and multilineage reconstitution after stem cell transplantation. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that loss of BCLAF1 reduces long-term HSCs and restrains expression of stress response genes. BCLAF1 associates with chromatin throughout the genome of fetal and adult hematopoietic cells to regulate transcriptional programs.

biological.citation: BCLAF1 binds SPOP to stabilize PD-L1 and promotes the development and immune escape of hepatocellular carcinoma. (PMID: 38340178)
biological.summary: BCLAF1 interacts with SPOP, an E3 ligase that mediates ubiquitination and degradation of PD-L1, competitively inhibiting SPOP-PD-L1 interaction and thereby stabilizing PD-L1 in hepatocellular carcinoma. An SPOP-binding consensus (SBC) motif on BCLAF1 mediates this interaction, and mutation of this motif disrupts regulation of the SPOP-PD-L1 axis. BCLAF1 expression was positively correlated with PD-L1 and negatively correlated with T cell activation markers CD3 and CD8 in HCC tissues.

biological.citation: Bclaf1 regulates c-FLIP expression and protects cells from TNF-induced apoptosis and tissue injury. (PMID: 34693625)
biological.summary: Bclaf1 was identified as a novel component of the anti-apoptotic program downstream of TNF signaling; Bclaf1 depletion sensitizes cells to TNF-induced apoptosis but not necroptosis. Bclaf1 promotes transcription of CFLAR (c-FLIP, a caspase-8 antagonist) by binding to the p50 subunit of NF-κB. In vivo, Bclaf1 siRNA-administered mice showed significantly more severe TNF-induced small intestine injury with aggravated apoptosis and pyroptosis.

biological.citation: Targeting the BCKDK/BCLAF1/MYC/HK2 axis to alter aerobic glycolysis and overcome Trametinib resistance in lung cancer. (PMID: 40442441)
biological.summary: BCKDK interacts with BCLAF1 and promotes its phosphorylation at serine 285, which facilitates BCLAF1 binding to the MYC promoter to enhance MYC transcription in lung cancer cells. Elevated MYC subsequently upregulates hexokinase 2, promoting aerobic glycolysis and Trametinib resistance. This BCKDK/BCLAF1/MYC/HK2 axis was identified through molecular biology experiments integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data.

The balance between miR-194-5p and its target BCLAF1 regulates differentiation and survival of normal hematopoietic progenitors, and this balance is perturbed in acute myeloid leukemia, locking cells in an immature state. Treatment with the HDAC inhibitor SAHA or exogenous miR-194-5p re-sensitizes AML cells to differentiation and apoptosis by inducing BCLAF1 nuclear-cytosolic shuttling. The miR-194-5p/BCLAF1 balance was found deregulated in 60 primary AML patients and largely restored by ex vivo SAHA treatment.

biological.citation: Transfer of miR-877-3p via extracellular vesicles derived from dental pulp stem cells attenuates neuronal apoptosis and facilitates early neurological functional recovery after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury through the Bclaf1/P53 signaling pathway. (PMID: 38878918)
biological.summary: miR-877-3p, a key component of dental pulp stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles, directly targets Bclaf1 as confirmed by target prediction and dual-luciferase assay, mediating neuroprotection against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Inhibition of miR-877-3p or overexpression of Bclaf1 reversed the neuroprotective effects of DPSC-EVs. The study implicates the Bclaf1/P53 signaling pathway in neuronal apoptosis following ischemic injury.

biological.citation: BCLAF1 Regulates Osteoarthritic Cartilage Degradation Through Interaction with LAMTOR2. (PMID: 39990659)
biological.summary: BCLAF1 levels were increased in cartilage tissue from OA patients, aged and surgery-induced OA mice, and in primary chondrocytes treated with inflammatory cytokines. Knockdown of Bclaf1 in chondrocytes inhibited catabolic factor expression and apoptosis while promoting anabolic factor expression, and intra-articular injection of shBclaf1 adenovirus attenuated cartilage degradation in a mouse OA model. Immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry identified LAMTOR2 as a key mediator that regulates BCLAF1 nuclear translocation.

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - PgmNr 2660: Whole genome sequencing analysis reveals the contribution of rare deleterious variants in the development of coronary artery disease. (H. Ieki et al.)
biological.summary: Whole genome sequencing of 4,417 Japanese samples (1,781 myocardial infarction cases, 2,636 controls) identified a significant excess of rare loss-of-function variants in BCLAF1 among healthy controls compared to cases (0 in cases vs. 16 in controls), suggesting that rare LOF variants in BCLAF1 may be protective against coronary artery disease. This finding reached genome-wide significance in the rare variant burden analysis.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Capture Hi-C identifies compelling candidate causal genes and enhancers for multiple sclerosis in the 6q23 region. (P. Martin et al.)
biological.summary: Capture Hi-C analysis of chromatin interactions in T- and B-cell lines at the 6q23 pan-autoimmune locus identified BCLAF1 as a candidate causal gene for multiple sclerosis, with MS-associated SNPs showing long-range chromatin interactions with the BCLAF1 promoter. Bioinformatics analysis further refined the interacting SNPs to enhancer regions, with BCLAF1 identified as an actively transcribed target gene. This implicates BCLAF1 as a potential therapeutic target in MS and other autoimmune diseases.
